title: Standardize intake scoring for VPC/on-prem customer requests with air-gap exceptions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Engineering and Sales are receiving a high volume of ad-hoc requests for VPC/private (on-prem) deployments that involve networking constraints, upgrade/maintenance windows, and air-gapped environments. There is no consistent intake scoring or routing, causing long evaluation times, missed SLA expectations, and rework for infra teams.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable intake and prioritization rubric and intake form for Private/VPC/on-prem customer requests that: (1) quantifies networking complexity, upgrade constraints, and air-gapped requirements; (2) produces a triage outcome (self-serve advise, low-touch integration, enterprise engagement); and (3) provides clear handoff data for Eng/SRE/Legal.

Scope: Non-bug, customer-request triage for private deployments and network/upgrade/air-gap constraints. Excludes full procurement, contract negotiations, and custom engineering work orders that require SOWs; these will be routed after prioritization.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page intake form template created and validated with Sales and Solutions Engineering
A scoring rubric that outputs one of three outcomes: green (self-serve guidance), amber (requires Dedicated offering + standard playbooks), red (enterprise engineering engagement + custom plan)
Automation/Gateway: mapping rules documented for routing to Slack channel (#private-intake) and PM queue
Hand-off checklist defined for Eng/SRE including required artifacts (network diagram, upgrade cadence, A/C images, KMS/HSM needs)
Pilot: 3 incoming real customer requests triaged through the rubric and time-to-first-response measured
comments: 2026-03-02 - AK: Kickoff with Solutions Eng and Sales. Common ask patterns: static IP requirements, restricted egress, locked-down bastion, OS image control, upgrade blackout windows for regulated customers. Agreement to capture a single "minimal network diagram" requirement.

2026-03-04 - LM: Drafted initial scoring rubric. Scores assigned for 5 categories: network topology complexity, egress control level, upgrade tolerances, data sovereignty, KMS/HSM requirement. Proposed thresholds for green/amber/red. Shared with ENG-2110 and SEC-76 for feedback.

2026-03-06 - SEC-76 (comment): Security wants an explicit field for 'required attestations' (e.g., FedRAMP/ISO controls) and a mandatory initial indicator if the deployment requires no public egress. This impacts whether we can provide prebuilt images.

2026-03-08 - LM: Updated intake form to include 'maintenance windows' with options: flexible (>=2 weeks), constrained (monthly windows), strict (>=6 months blackout). Noted that strict blackouts push to a red outcome. Added example network diagram template link.

2026-03-10 - AK: Sales provided three intake examples from recent customers. Ran rubric on examples: two amber, one red. Time to triage reduced from ~5 business days to ~24 hours during the mock run. Need to confirm with Eng availability for amber queue.

2026-03-11 - LM: Scoped pilot automation: Zapier/Forms -> GitHub issue template -> Slack notification to #private-intake. Engineering to confirm SLO for first response (24h) for amber/red. Open question: Do we require a signed NDA before sharing detailed network diagrams?
2026-03-12 - AK: Leadership review scheduled. Requested that LM include an 'estimated engineering effort range' field to help Sales set expectations (0-8h, 1-3 days, 2+ weeks).
decisions: Use a 3-tier outcome for triage: green/amber/red (no partial states)
Include 'maintenance blackout window' as a high-weight factor in scoring (x2 multiplier)
All red outcomes require Security + SRE signoff before starting any custom work
Pilot automation will leverage internal forms and a GH issue template; full productization deferred to a Dashboard in console-2026.2
next_steps: LM to finalize rubric and publish Confluence intake doc (link below) - due 2026-03-15
AK to coordinate pilot with Sales and Solutions Eng; pick 3 live requests - due 2026-03-18
ENG-2110 (Networking) to confirm acceptance criteria for amber queue and available on-call slots - due 2026-03-16
SEC-76 to confirm NDA/attestation requirement language - due 2026-03-14
Follow-up review with leadership after pilot and recommend rollout plan - due 2026-03-26
notes: Trade-offs: A highly granular intake improves accuracy but increases friction for Sales. We opted for a concise form with a mandatory minimal diagram and a couple high-weight fields (blackout windows, no-egress).
Edge cases: Air-gapped requests that also require KMS/HSM and approved images will likely be multi-week engagements; mark as red by default and attach SOW path.
Metrics: track time-to-triage, percent of requests per outcome, average engineering hours per amber outcome.
